c0006: ▸ Complete checklist for the daily opening and closing of your chocolate shop or kitchen.
c0007: ▸ Covers tempering equipment start-up, display cases, shop setup and closing.
c0012: ▸ Print on US Letter and keep it in the kitchen and at the counter.
c0014: ▸ The first section of "Opening" is personal hygiene and a safe start: exhaust fan first, gas check next (if you have gas equipment), and only then the tempering machine, display cases and climate control.
c0015: ▸ The cool room and fridges are not "turned on": check that they ran all night and log the reading. Targets for this trade: kitchen 64–68 °F, cool room 59–64 °F at 50–60% humidity, fillings and ganaches 41 °F or below, bonbon display case 60–64 °F.
c0016: ▸ Above 68 °F cocoa butter starts to melt: the bonbon sweats, loses its shine and within two days fat bloom shows up. That is why the display case gets its own check.
c0022: Personal hygiene and safe kitchen start-up
c0028: Clean uniform and work shoes, fresh apron, hair tied back under a cap or hairnet
c0030: No rings (a plain band is OK), bracelets, watch or dangling earrings; nails short and clean, no polish or false nails
c0031: Wash hands with soap and dry with a single-use paper towel, and again at every change of task (finished chocolate has no step left that kills pathogens)
c0033: Anyone with vomiting, diarrhea, fever or infected skin lesions does NOT handle product: tell the shift lead and reassign the task
c0034: Turn on the kitchen exhaust fan BEFORE any other equipment
c0035: If the kitchen has gas equipment: check there is no gas smell, then light it (the main valve stays open; know where it is)
c0037: Turn on the tempering machine and preheat to 113 °F
c0039: Check the cool room ran all night (no outages or alarms) and log the temperature: target 59–64 °F and 50–60% humidity — log reading: ____ °F
c0041: Check the fillings and ganache fridge ran all night and log the temperature: target 41 °F or below — log reading: ____ °F
c0043: Turn on display case lighting and shop floor lights
c0045: Check the bonbon display case holds 60–64 °F and is not fogging up before setting out product (above 68 °F cocoa butter melts and bonbons lose their shine) — log reading: ____ °F
c0046: Turn on the A/C — keep the shop at 68–72 °F
c0048: Log kitchen, cool room and fridge temperatures: in the temperature log of the HACCP Food Safety Kit Pro if you have it; if not, right here in "Notes"
c0051: Set up the display case: bonbons, bars, molded figures, truffles
c0052: Check the label on every item on display: product name, price (and price per lb if sold by weight) and declared allergens (milk, egg, wheat, soy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame; UK: 14 allergens) plus any "may contain" statements
c0053: Restock bags, gift boxes, tissue paper, ribbons
c0055: Check stock of assorted bonbon gift boxes
c0056: Set up the sample station with the day's samples
c0058: Check the POS is active and the starting bank was already counted and logged before you unlock the door: no recount here, it is done on the "Cash Drawer Opening" tab of file 09 (milestone in files 08/09)
c0060: Put out the chalkboard with new items and featured products
c0063: Check the display case glass is clean
c0064: Confirm online orders waiting to be prepared
c0065: Review the calendar: special orders, events, pre-orders
c0074: Take product out of the display case and store it in the cool room
c0075: Cover any bonbons left out with plastic wrap
c0076: Check the day's cash count is closed and signed and sales are recorded: the reconcile is not repeated here, it is done on the "Cash Drawer Closing" tab of file 09 (milestone in files 08/09)
c0077: Check the POS and card terminal are closed AFTER the cash count, never before: the terminal batch is sent on the "Shop Closing" tab of file 08 (milestone in files 08/09)
c0078: Clean and sanitize counters and display case glass
c0080: Clean and dry the tempering machine
c0081: Wash used molds and leave them to dry
c0083: Store open couverture in airtight containers
c0085: Check and log temperatures before closing: cool room 59–64 °F and fillings fridge 41 °F or below — log readings: ____ °F / ____ °F
c0087: Log the day's waste: product, quantity and reason (breakage, bad temper, bloom, expiry, samples or test batch)
c0088: Sweep and mop the kitchen floor
c0091: Turn off equipment except the cool room and fridges
c0093: Make sure gas burners are off (the main valve is for emergencies only) and that water and lights are off

c0102: ▸ Control of craft production: tempering, molding, bonbons, bars.
c0103: ▸ Log batches, temperatures and times for each process.
c0104: ▸ Adapt the base recipes to your own formulas.
c0105: ▸ Set temper temps by couverture, per the manufacturer's curve.
c0106: ▸ Print and keep in the kitchen next to the tempering machine.
c0108: ▸ Before tempering, check the kitchen AIR: 64–68 °F and 50–60% humidity. The three couverture curves on this sheet only work inside that window.
c0109: ▸ At the bottom of "Molding & Bars" is an editable shelf life table by product type: adjust it to your formula. It sits outside the counter because it is a reference, not a task.
c0110: ▸ Finished chocolate is NEVER frozen: it condenses on thawing, the water dissolves surface sugar and leaves sugar bloom. Only bulk ganache can be frozen.
c0116: Check kitchen temperature and humidity BEFORE tempering: target 64–68 °F and 50–60% humidity (warmer than that, the cocoa butter will not crystallize and bloom appears) — log reading: ____ °F
c0117: Weigh couverture per the day's production order
c0118: Chop the couverture and load it into the tempering machine
c0121: Cool to 81–82 °F on the marble slab or by seeding
c0123: Tempering test on a spatula tip: it should set in 3–5 min at 68 °F, with shine, a clean snap and shrinkage in the mold. If not, remelt and retemper — never mold "and hope for the best"
c0124: Log batch, time and final temperature
c0127: Cool to 79–81 °F on the marble slab or by seeding
c0129: Tempering test, thin layer on paper: at 64–68 °F it should set in 3–5 min, with even shine and no streaks, starting from the working temperature of 84–86 °F. If not, remelt and retemper — never mold "and hope for the best". Log the batch, time and final temperature
c0132: Cool to 77–79 °F on the marble slab or by seeding
c0134: Tempering test, thin layer on paper: at 64–68 °F it should set in 3–5 min, with even shine and no streaks, starting from the working temperature of 82–84 °F. If not, remelt and retemper — never mold "and hope for the best". Log the batch, time and final temperature
c0137: Prep clean molds at room temperature (68–72 °F)
c0138: Pour tempered chocolate into the molds — tap to remove air bubbles
c0139: Pour out the excess — leave an even shell of 1/16–1/8 in
c0140: Invert molds over a rack and let drain
c0142: Prepare the day's fillings/ganaches per recipe
c0143: Fill bonbons to 80%, leaving room for the cap
c0144: Cap with tempered chocolate — smooth with a spatula
c0145: Chill 15–20 min until the chocolate contracts
c0146: Unmold, check shine and store on trays
c0148: Prep clean bar molds at room temperature
c0150: Add inclusions if needed: nuts, dried fruit, salt
c0151: Smooth the surface with a spatula
c0153: Unmold, check the finish and weigh each bar
c0154: Wrap in paper/foil and label with lot and date
c0157: Check shine, texture and snap of products
c0158: Log production batches: product, quantity, date
c0159: Label each batch with its production date and best-by date by product type (table at the bottom of the sheet)
c0160: Log the day's waste: product, quantity and reason (breakage, bad temper, bloom, test). Plain chocolate that is uncontaminated can be remelted; anything with ganache or fruit goes in the trash
c0161: Store finished product at 59–64 °F and 50–60% humidity, in the dark and away from strong odors (cocoa absorbs them) — log reading: ____ °F
c0167: The enemy is not time: it is moisture, light and odors. Keep sealed and in the dark
c0170: Same as the bar, but a hollow piece cracks with sudden temperature changes
c0174: Bonbons with UHT cream, sorbate or alcohol
c0176: Preservative and alcohol lower water activity; without them you will not reach even half of this
c0179: Nut fat goes rancid and refrigeration does not prevent it: go by the date, not the look
c0182: If they contain cream or butter, count them as fresh ganache
c0185: Watch for sugar crystallization in the shell: it cracks and leaks
c0186: Candied nuts and chocolate-dipped candied fruit
c0188: They clump with moisture; airtight packaging with a desiccant if your kitchen is humid
c0190: They lose their crunch long before they become unsafe: pull them for quality
c0193: On thawing it condenses, the water dissolves surface sugar and leaves sugar bloom. Only bulk ganache can be frozen, at 0 °F or below for 1–2 months, thawed 24 h in the fridge and unopened
